summary: Airborne and among the most contagious viral diseases known - secondary attack rate >=90% in susceptible household/institutional contacts. Prodrome of fever (up to 105F), malaise, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, then pathognomonic Koplik spots, then maculopapular rash (~14 days post-exposure). 20% of US cases are hospitalized; ~1 encephalitis case and 2-3 deaths per 1,000 reported cases. No FDA-approved antiviral exists - management is supportive care only. Vitamin A is a supportive adjunct, not a treatment or vaccine substitute. Contagious 4 days before to 4 days after rash onset; isolate 4 days post-rash if immunocompetent, for duration of illness if immunocompromised (prolonged shedding). (CDC Clinical Overview of Measles)

news.what: 4,080 confirmed US measles cases, 42 outbreaks, 96% outbreak-associated year-to-date (as of 2026-10-08) - worst year since the early 1990s.
Full-year 2025: 2,289 confirmed US cases, 48 outbreaks, 90% outbreak-associated.
